title: Latest estimate for Starship launches required to support a Moon landing? 22.
gist: NASA's Aerospace Safety Advisory Panel member Charlie Precourt said the latest estimate is about 22 Starship flights to fuel a Starship lunar lander, up from NASA's earlier "high single digits to the low double digits". Elon Musk called that "way too high" and said 6 to 8. Berger notes that even at twice-weekly launches by end-2027, fueling a depot would take about three months, which raises doubts about Starship's role in a 2028 Artemis landing.

insights.claim: NASA safety panel member Charlie Precourt said the latest estimate for refueling flights needed for the Starship lunar lander is around 22. NASA's earlier figures were "high single digits to the low double digits" (about a dozen) from former HLS director Lisa Watson-Morgan, and other officials had said "high teens".

insights.so_what: Rising tanker counts make the Artemis lunar landing more complex and costly and point to a later timeline for SpaceX's HLS contract.

insights.speaker: Eric Berger
insights.so_what: How quickly Starship's payload capacity improves is the key variable for tanker count and Artemis timing.
